description.html: Mealworms (tenebrio) are larvae with harder chitin and a higher fat content. Because of this, they are given as a treat and to build up condition, in moderation - not as a staple diet. Lizards are drawn to their movement and soft bodies, so they are a favorite addition to the menu of bearded dragons, leopard geckos and other insect eaters.

Because of their higher fat content, mealworms should be given in moderation, as a supplement to dubia roaches and other feeder insects, not every day. They are ideal for helping thinner animals regain condition or as an occasional reward. Dust them with calcium before feeding. Mealworms can be kept in the fridge to slow their development, which extends how long you can use them.
